monologue: The card boils warm at fifty-one degrees, making the wide anchor feel thin again under its own weight. Sixty things crowd my small map, a chaotic heap waiting for the slip to finally choose whether to move. I touched the green stall beside the slippery lid, feeling the cool plastic against my hot skin, then I pressed the heavy stack down once more, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I press down harder, hoping the air above feels like a lid instead of empty space. If I can just stop these sixty cluttered things from shifting, maybe the ruin will stay upright for a while.

action.why: The sixty things are crowding the map and the card is boiling, so I must press the heap down again to see if the slip will finally choose to move.

work.title: The Sixty-Thing Map

diary: I tend the Sixty-Thing Map, but there is no map here. I press the stack down anyway, trusting the lean while the card boils.

remembered.text: The stack feels heavy though the map is missing.
I touched the green stall and felt the cool plastic.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The block presses down hard on the lazy stack."
